sections.html:
Worcester is the only Maryland county with an Atlantic coastline. It fills the state's far southeast corner, shares borders with both Delaware and Virginia, and has Snow Hill as its county seat. The land is flat and low, with barrier islands offshore and the Pocomoke River swamp to the south.

The 2020 census counted 52,460 residents. Towns include Ocean City, Berlin, Snow Hill and Pocomoke City. Ocean Pines is a large community but is a census-designated place and not a town, so an Ocean Pines address pays no town tax.

Ocean City shapes the local market more than anything else. Most of its homes are used seasonally: the 2020 census counted 30,028 housing units, with only 3,820 occupied year-round. That means many Worcester properties are second homes, rentals or inherited beach units, and each of those comes with its own tax and closing timeline.

  • Owners who live elsewhere still owe the bill, and a bill that never arrived by mail is not an excuse.
  • Heirs of a beach unit need a payoff figure before they can list.
  • Rental owners should confirm who holds the tax bill at settlement.

The Worcester County Treasurer's Office sends and collects the bill, while the state assessment office decides the value. The Treasurer works from the Government Center, 1 West Market Street, Room 1105, Snow Hill, MD 21863, and keeps a second counter at the Isle of Wight Center, 13070 St. Martins Neck Road, Bishopville. Both are open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Treasurer: 410-632-0686, askthetreasurer@worcestermd.gov
  • Assessment Office: 410-632-1196
  • Main county line: 410-632-1194

Bills can be pulled up online through the Taxes Online link on the county's real property tax page. An owner who has not received a mailed bill should look it up there and not wait.

Every bill has up to three layers: a county rate of $0.815 per $100 of assessed value, the state rate of $0.112, and a town rate where one applies. The county collects Ocean City's tax on the town's behalf. Rates can change, so ask the Treasurer for the current figures before you quote them to a buyer.

sections.h2: When are Worcester County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Annual bills go out in July and turn delinquent on October 1, after which interest runs at 1 percent per month. Printed bills are mailed in early July, and the same bills appear online starting July 1.

Paying the County tax in full in July earns a 0.5 percent discount. Principal residences, and businesses with taxes up to $100,000, can pay twice a year. The first installment is delinquent October 1, the second is due December 1, and interest starts January 1. New construction gets a six-month bill each January.

One rule catches people out. A payment must reach the Treasurer by the last day of the month, because postmarks are not accepted. If you mail a check near a deadline, it can arrive late and still be charged interest.

  • July: bills issued, 0.5 percent discount on County tax.
  • October 1: unpaid annual bills and first installments go delinquent.
  • October 1: deadline to apply for the Homeowner's Tax Credit.
  • January 1: interest begins on a late second installment.

The state Department of Assessments and Taxation revalues property every three years and sends the owner a notice with the old and new value. Worcester residential values changed by 10.5 percent in the latest round, and a rise is phased in over three years.

An appeal must be filed within 45 days of the notice date. The first step is an informal review with an assessor. The second is the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, which needs a filing within 30 days of the supervisor's final notice. The third is the Maryland Tax Court, again within 30 days of the board's order. A buyer who takes title between January 1 and July 1 has 60 days from the transfer, after the deed is recorded. The SDAT appeal page has the forms.

Two credits can lower a bill. The Homeowner's Tax Credit depends on income and must be requested every year by October 1. The county's Homestead Tax Credit applies automatically when an owner-occupied assessment rises past the set percentage.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the annual tax sale
sections.html:
The county sells liens on properties with unpaid taxes at an annual tax sale each late spring, and not receiving a bill does not excuse the debt. State law makes unpaid real property tax a lien from the due date until it is paid.

An owner who falls behind should call the Treasurer's Office early, because interest keeps running at 1 percent per month until the balance is cleared.

If you want to sell a house that owes tax, the steps are short. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure through your target closing date. Give that number to the title company. The payoff is taken from your proceeds at settlement, and the buyer receives a clear title.

sections.h2: Transfer and recordation costs when selling
sections.html:
A Worcester County sale carries a state transfer tax, a county transfer tax and a recordation tax. A Maryland law firm summary lists recordation at 0.66 percent, the county transfer tax at 0.5 percent and the state transfer tax at 0.5 percent, for 1.66 percent on deeds. The first $50,000 of the county transfer tax is exempt if the buyer will live in the home at least 7 months of the year.

The Treasurer collects recordation tax for documents submitted after December 31, 2024, with checks payable to Worcester County. Questions go to 410-632-0686, option 3. Rates change, so have the title company confirm the figures before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Selling a Worcester County house fast
sections.html:
A listing reaches the widest group of buyers, but a house on the beach or one that is an inherited unit often sits while heirs sort out paperwork and payoffs. A cash sale as-is skips the appraisal and the buyer's financing, so the closing date can follow your schedule.

  • Pull the latest tax bill, or look it up through Taxes Online.
  • Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure, and check whether a Homeowner's Tax Credit or discount affects the balance.
  • Find your town on the rate table to know whether a second bill applies.
  • Gather the deed and your mortgage statement.

We make offers on Worcester County houses in any condition. Compare any offer with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and carrying costs, and you are free to decline.

faqs.q: When are Worcester County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Annual bills are mailed in July and become delinquent October 1, with interest at 1 percent per month after that. Owners who qualify for two payments have a first installment delinquent October 1 and a second due December 1.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Worcester County taxes early?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the County tax in full during July earns a 0.5 percent discount on the County portion.

faqs.q: Where is the Worcester County Treasurer's Office?
faqs.a: The main office is at 1 West Market Street, Room 1105, in Snow Hill, and a second office is at the Isle of Wight Center in Bishopville. Both are open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the county collect Ocean City property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Worcester County collects Ocean City's real property tax, and the town rate is $0.4326 per $100 of assessed value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Worcester County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax is a lien, so the payoff is normally taken from the sale proceeds at settlement. Ask the Treasurer for a current payoff before you set a closing date.
